title: Staged schema-hint migration + manifest fencing reconciler for on-prem upgrade stall and tenant config skew
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Several customers running on-prem Private deployments observed stalled operator rolling upgrades accompanied by per-tenant configuration divergence. This ticket captures the triage, temporary mitigations, and a proposed staged schema-hint migration plus manifest-fencing reconciler to safely repair tenant state without data loss or extended downtime.
description: Background: During a multi-cluster rolling upgrade of the operator (hosted control plane upgrade to operator-2.14.0), a subset of tenants reported long-running reconcile stalls (controller loop stuck for >15m) and manifest parity mismatches (desired CR spec != cluster live object). Support escalations show tenants with customer-facing outages on Dedicated/Private environments. Prior hotpatch attempts reduced symptoms but did not address root cause. This ticket defines investigation findings, temporary mitigations used in customer escalations, and a low-risk long-term fix: a staged schema-hint migration plus a manifest-fencing reconciler that can be run per-tenant to prevent destructive writes and enable deterministic repair.
root_cause_hypothesis: Operator upgrade introduces batched CRD apply path that triggers non-deterministic field ordering in controller indexing combined with leader-election rebalancing. For tenants with high manifest churn (external tools writing status/annotations concurrently) we observe transient resource versions that cause the reconciler to drop KV cache keys and re-apply partial manifests, resulting in 'shadowing' (field-level skew) and eventual reconcile stalls. The controller logs show repeated optimistic concurrency conflicts and backoff loops for affected tenant namespaces.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Prepare on-prem cluster with operator v2.13.x and a tenant namespace with heavy config rotation (eg. CI/CD tooling updating ConfigMaps/Secrets every 5s).
2) Start rolling upgrade of operator to v2.14.0 across controller replicas with leader-election enabled and short lease durations.
3) Simulate concurrent writes to a custom resource schema with many nullable fields and annotations churn.
4) Observe reconcile loop for tenant CR frequently failing with conflict errors and some fields diverging between desired vs live. Logs indicate skipped KV cache entries and repeated apply attempts.
observed_logs: error: failed to apply patch: conflict: resourceVersion mismatch (requested 1024, current 1027)
warn: kv-cache: missing prefix key for tenant=tenant-42, falling back to full diff
info: leader-election: new leader elected replica-3 at 2026-03-11T14:22:03Z
error: reconcile loop exceeded retry budget, entering extended backoff for namespace tenant-42
immediate_mitigations: 1) For affected customers we paused automated manifest writers (CI/CD) where possible to reduce churn.
2) Performed targeted operator replica restart to break stuck leader election and force KV cache refresh for tenant namespaces.
3) Applied conservative manual 'seal' patch to live manifests to record last-known-good spec in an annotation to avoid blind rewrites.
4) Opened support communication thread with impacted customers and scheduled maintenance windows for per-tenant repair.
proposed_fix_summary: Implement a two-part repair: (A) a staged 'schema-hint' migration that records canonical field ordering and type hints in the CRD controller layer to make patch application deterministic across replicas; (B) a manifest-fencing reconciler that, when enabled for a tenant, creates a transactional fence annotation and replays a verified three-way merge between desired, live, and last-known-good to repair field-level skew without losing ephemeral fields.
design_notes: - Schema-hint: lightweight metadata persisted in operator's leader-only store and used to normalize serialization order for CRs during apply.

- Fencing reconciler: introduces fence annotation 'inference.redwood.io/fence-v=YYYYMMDDHHMM' to mark repair windows. While fenced, external writers receive 409s for controller-managed fields to avoid race writes.
- Reconciler will perform per-field timestamp comparisons and favor last-known-good for non-customer-provided ephemeral annotations.
- All repairs logged with reconcile-run id for audit and can be rolled back by reapplying prior annotation.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag operator binary with schema-hint migration disabled by default. Deploy to canary infra (internal staging) and run upgrade test harness against churn-producing workloads.
Phase 1: Enable schema-hint migration only (no fencing) in 2 clusters, monitor for reduced conflicts for 48h.
Phase 2: Gradually enable manifest-fencing reconciler as opt-in annotation for customers who consent to repair. Run reconciler in dry-run first, produce audit logs for review.
Phase 3: For consenting tenants, run live repair during scheduled maintenance window; keep fencing annotation for 30min post-repair to prevent immediate churn.
Phase 4: If stable for 72h, flip feature flag on for all operator-managed tenants and remove temporary fencing after telemetry confirms parity.
canary_criteria: Conflict error rate for canary tenants drops by >=80% within 24h.
No data-loss incidents or 5xx customer API errors introduced by reconciler.
All reconciler dry-runs must produce a verified manifest delta report and be approved by SRE and PM before live run.
rollback_plan: If reconciler causes unintended deletions or regressions: (1) immediately annotate affected tenant with 'inference.redwood.io/repair-rollback' and suspend reconciler; (2) reapply last-known-good spec from auditing annotation; (3) restart operator replicas with feature flag off; (4) open emergency PR to revert migration code and trigger patch release.
Keep snapshot backups of affected tenant manifests in GCS/Artifact store with timestamped keys for quick restore.
monitoring_and_alerting_changes: Add alert: reconcile_backoff_spike if tenants with fencing enabled show >10x backoff compared to baseline for 15m
Add dashboard: per-tenant field-drift heatmap (shows number of fields differing between desired/live)
communication_template: Support note to customers: "We detected upgrade-induced reconcile contention in your tenant and will perform a controlled repair that avoids data loss. We request a 30-minute maintenance window and will run the repair in dry-run first, share the delta report, and only proceed with your approval. Contact support for scheduling."
postmortem_actions: 1) Add upgrade preflight test to upgrade harness that simulates high manifest churn for each release candidate.
2) Add an operator-level pre-upgrade telemetry check that warns if >5% of tenants have heavy churn and blocks automatic rolling upgrade unless overridden.
3) Document per-tenant repair runbook and approval checklist for Support/SE teams.
4) Schedule a knowledge-transfer session with Solutions Eng to walk through fencing reconciler behavior.
notes: We must keep customer-facing messaging conservative: emphasize repair safety and auditability. Target for completing code, tests, and dry-run reviews is EOW 2026-03-20. Coordinate with legal if any tenant manifests include PII before snapshot storage.
